text:
cassie (product): Dropping a synopsis from the customer roadmap workshop. We need a single "decision path" for isolation + routing that teams can act on. Customers want: predictable tail latency, a clear pricing delta, and a safe cutover path.

hoshi (eng-plat): Agreed. My take: convert asks into 3 deliverables in priority order: 1) policy engine + observable fallback (low risk), 2) reservation model (soft/hard) + billing enforcement, 3) private control plane for VPC/on-prem. Each deliverable gets gates + abort criteria.

amar (infra): Implementation nuance: reservations can be implemented as either dedicated pools (nodes carved out per tenant) or reservation tokens on shared capacity (eviction mechanics). Dedicated pools = clean guarantees but higher ops cost. Token model = cheaper but harder to reason about tail latency.

maria (sre): Ops work: we need a standard chaos matrix for each model. Example: Token model chaos = force 20% spike and assert p99 remainder < 2x baseline and user error rate < 0.3%. Also add an automated detection rule for cross-region spill and a throttle for non-critical traffic.

ben (sales): FinSecure and HealthCo care about contract language. They want a priced SKU that maps to an SLA. Sales wants a one-pager showing price multiplier -> expected p95/p99 improvements and a migration credit for early signups.

research-bot: Quick note: model quantization interacts with kernel selection; some quantized variants increase token latency under certain kernels. Will publish compat matrix by Tue.

hoshi (eng-plat): API sketch for a simple policy: `redwood policy apply --tenant T --tier reserved --regions eu-west-1,us-east-1 --fallback nearest` Console should show estimated cost and expected latency band. Also add telemetry event `policy.fallback` with fields tenant, fallback_model, latency_ms, origin_region.

cassie (product): For cutover gates, I'm proposing:
- gate A (policy): policy API live + soft-affinity on 5% canary; telemetry visible + p95 < 150ms in perf harness.
- gate B (reservation-token): billing hooks + quota enforcement; canary with 2 paying customers; chaos scenario pass.
- gate C (dedicated pools/private): contract signed, warm-buffer validated, install/runbook for private.
Gates include abort triggers (SLO regressions, >10% cost delta, quality drop).

amar (infra): Warm-buffer idea: keep N warm slots per reserved pool to avoid cold-starts. That must be priced. We'll run cost sims to recommend N per tenant profile.

maria (sre): I'll produce abort criteria and runbooks. Also recommend an automated rollback that removes reservation and falls back to shared lane if p99 > threshold. Need explicit instrumentation to detect user-impacting errors vs degraded perf.

billing-bot: FYI: billing hooks required: per-tenant quota enforcement with 60s enforcement window and overage alerting. Need finance to define overage pricing band.

ben (sales): Can we offer two reservation pricing options: Commit-Monthly (lower unit price) vs Burstable-Reserved (higher base but credits for unused)? Sales wants that to negotiate enterprise pilots.

hoshi (eng-plat): Dependency list: research (compat matrix), runtime (warm-start + kernel gating), infra (pool allocator + egress caps), billing (quota APIs), console (policy UI + estimator). Need owners for each.

cassie (product): I'll draft the decision doc with these gates and the one-pager. Proposed reviewers: hoshi, amar, maria, ben, and finance. Deadline: Friday COB.

research-bot: Added action: publish model compatibility matrix by Tue EOD.

amar (infra): Action: I'll run cost sims for three tenant profiles and post numbers to /shared/cost-sims/1807654321 in ~48h. Will include warm-buffer suggestions.

maria (sre): Action: I'll create the chaos matrix and schedule a red-team eviction run against a staging reservation-token implementation.

ben (sales): Action: I'll draft the price-vs-latency one-pager and propose the migration credit structure.

cassie (product): Any other blockers? If not I'll start the PR and tag owners.

hoshi (eng-plat): One more: add a quality gate for fallback: we run a small eval prompt set on fallback model and require delta < 3% on key metrics. If >= 3% we disable automatic fallback and fail-over to nearest compatible region only.

cassie (product): Noted 94 will add that to the acceptance criteria. PR incoming.

billing-bot: Reminder: include test endpoints for billing hooks so QA can validate enforcement during canary.

amar (infra): No more from infra. We'll sync on capacity numbers tomorrow.

maria (sre): I'll TL;DR the runbook after chaos runs.

cassie (product): Thanks all 94 turning this into the decision doc now. Will ping for review.
